parts: Pollution is the addition of any substance to the environment in excess of what is normally present, making it impure (from Latin 'polluere', to contaminate). Substances that cause pollution are pollutants: a constituent in the wrong amount, at the wrong place or at the wrong time, e.g. dust, dirt, garbage, chemicals and industrial waste. Pollution is classed as air, water, soil and noise pollution.

Plants give out oxygen by day and use carbon dioxide, balancing the air. Sources: combustion (household fuel, coal in power stations, vehicle exhaust, crackers, factory smoke), industry, agriculture (spraying pesticides and insecticides), solvents and spray paints; natural sources are volcanoes, forest fires and wind-blown dust. Effects: eye infections, respiratory allergies, bronchitis and asthma, skin allergies; plants get less sunlight, their leaf pores are blocked and food production falls; poor visibility and smog cause accidents; rise in temperature and destruction of vegetation (e.g. the Gulf War oil fires).

Control: smokeless chulha with a tall chimney, biogas, solar cooker, chimney filters in factories, factories far from residential areas, devices on vehicles, unleaded petrol and CNG, do not burn garbage (use sanitary landfill), pucca roads, plant and care for trees, grow crops all year so soil is not exposed to erosion.

Safe water has no taste, smell, colour, dirt or germs. Sources of pollution: domestic wastes (washing clothes, bathing animals, washing after defecation, garbage thrown in water), industrial wastes (toxic), agricultural wastes (fertiliser and pesticide run-off), and oil spills. Effects: cholera, typhoid, diarrhoea, dysentery and hepatitis from drinking; skin diseases from bathing; fish and water plants die for lack of oxygen. Control: no untreated sewage or industrial waste in water sources; use latrines; keep latrines, soakage pits, dumping grounds and landfills away from water; no bathing or washing clothes near water sources (harvest rain water for this); no garbage in rivers and seas; a concrete parapet and pucca floor around wells and ponds; store water in clean covered containers and use a long-handled ladle.

Soil pollution is a change in the physical, chemical and biological nature of soil harmful to living beings. Causes: industrial chemicals and metals, excess insecticides, pesticides and fertilisers, rotting garbage that breeds insects and germs, open defecation and urination, spitting. Walking barefoot on such soil lets germs and worms enter the body. Control: proper disposal of garbage in covered bins; dumping pits outside the city covered with soil; sanitary landfills; composting garden waste into manure; incineration (latest technology, expensive but sterile, reduces garbage to ash); burning refuse is banned in metros because of smoke; sanitary latrines, limited use of pesticides and fertilisers and use of Eco-mark (environment-friendly) products.

Any unpleasant sound is noise. Sources: automobiles, trains and aircraft; loudspeakers, radio and TV at full volume; industries and machines. Effects: disturbance, nervous strain, headache, mental disturbance and stress, loss of hearing and deafness (factory workers, pilots, drivers). Control: radio and TV at low volume, avoid loudspeakers, talk in low tones, horns only when necessary, silencers in vehicles, factories and airports away from residential areas.
